questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the practical difference between 'the model works' and 'the model is documented'?
options: They mean exactly the same thing and are interchangeable claims
'The model works' is a claim about behavior; a model card is what lets someone else verify that claim without re-running every eval themselves
Documentation is only needed for models that don't work correctly
A documented model never needs to be evaluated again
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes a behavioral claim from the documentation that lets someone else independently verify it rather than taking it on faith.

questions.q: Where does this lesson say the model card format actually originates from?
options: It was invented specifically for this course and has no prior history
A 2019 research paper by Margaret Mitchell and coauthors at Google, which has since become close to a de facto industry standard
A government regulation that mandates its exact wording
It was first created by Hugging Face as a marketing tool
questions.explain: The lesson cites the 2019 'Model Cards for Model Reporting' paper as the origin, noting it has become close to a de facto standard, including on Hugging Face's hub.

questions.q: What does the 'Intended Use' section of a model card actually do, per this lesson?
options: It changes the model's underlying code and behavior automatically
It explicitly states what a model is for and what it was NOT evaluated or approved for, which can cheaply prevent a known pattern of real-world harm
It is a purely decorative section with no practical effect
It replaces the need for any evaluation results in the rest of the card
questions.explain: The lesson explains that writing explicit non-uses (like 'not evaluated for medical advice') closes off a category of foreseeable misuse at the cost of one sentence.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a model card should be treated as a 'living document' rather than a one-time artifact?
options: A model card written at launch and never updated goes stale once the model is retrained or drift is detected, making it no longer trustworthy
Model cards automatically update themselves without any human involvement
Once written, a model card never needs any further changes under any circumstances
Living documents are a requirement only for open-source models
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns that an unmaintained model card can become inaccurate the moment the model's real behavior or status changes.

questions.q: Which of these does this lesson list as an actual section of a real model card?
options: A list of every individual user who has ever queried the model
The model's current stock price and market valuation
Evaluation Results — pulling real metrics from the kind of evals built earlier in this course
A full transcript of every support ticket ever filed
questions.explain: The lesson lists Model Details, Intended Use, Training Data, Evaluation Results, Ethical Considerations, and Caveats & Limitations as the real sections of a model card.
